g.text: ↳ zagg (DGGS, generalizing) · xagg (polygon zones) · geopandas sjoin+groupby
L²-projection from mesh basis → target basis
linear — encodable as sparse matrix W (precomputable)
family has both linear and nonlinear methods
global support — needs full target grid
Reprojection changes CRS; pixels stay pixels. Family 1 (kernel convolution) is sufficient.
Regridding changes grid structure (size, topology). Family 1 is rarely the right answer.
Categorical data (land cover, classifications) → Family 1 nearest or Family 4 mode; never bilinear/cubic.
Linear methods encode as a sparse weight matrix W and apply as output = W·input.
Cached W amortizes across time steps & variables — xESMF / grid-weights pattern.
Nonlinear methods (mode, median, max…) precompute only indexing, not the operator.
That's why grid-indexing is a standalone library from grid-weights.
